title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 239
paragraphs: I will now return to the point in my narrative where I left off. The Lacedaemonians had been informed before all others that the king was preparing an expedition against Greece, and so they sent to the oracle at Delphi, where that reply was given them which I reported shortly before. They got this information in a strange way. Demaratos son of Ariston, after fleeing for refuge to the Medes, was not friendly to the Lacedaemonians — such is my opinion, which likelihood supports — but whether he did what follows out of goodwill or out of malicious triumph over them, it is open to anyone to conjecture. When Xerxes had decided to make a campaign against Greece, Demaratos, being in Susa and having been informed of it, wished to report it to the Lacedaemonians. He could find no other way to send the news without being discovered, but he contrived as follows: he took a folding tablet, scraped off the wax that was on it, and then wrote the king's plan on the wood of the tablet itself; after doing so, he melted the wax and poured it back over the writing, so that the tablet (being carried with apparently no writing on it) would not cause trouble with the keepers of the road. When it arrived at Lacedaemon, the Lacedaemonians could not make sense of it, until at last, as I am told, Gorgo, daughter of Cleomenes and wife of Leonidas, suggested a plan she herself had thought of, telling them to scrape the wax and they would find writing on the wood. Doing as she said, they found the writing and read it, and after that they sent word to the other Greeks. These events, it is said, came to pass in this way.
